title: Spring warmth gave no clear link to missing first-bloom dates in four US plant samples from 1965 to 2008
abstract: We tested whether February-March warmth was linked to a missing first-bloom date when a first-leaf date was recorded. We used 15,705 repeated US lilac and honeysuckle plant-years in four region-period samples from 1965 to 2008. Models had plant and year effects. Slopes ranged from -0.18 to +0.99 percentage points per C. All four intervals adjusted for four tests included zero. All 32 sensitivity intervals also included zero under the same rule within each variant. The records did not establish a common temperature link or random missingness. Wide intervals, unknown visit effort, different taxon mixtures, coarse weather, and selection on leaf reports limit inference. Missing dates cannot separate missed observations from a true lack of flowering. The package contains a reusable completeness panel, code, source hashes, all estimates, numerical checks, and a figure.

display.caption: Temperature slopes for missing first-bloom records conditional on a first-leaf record. Bars are four-test adjusted intervals. Missing records do not establish failure to flower.
